paper.title: The Hardness Analysis of Thompson Sampling for Combinatorial Semi-bandits with Greedy Oracle

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with Greedy oracle (semi-bandit feedback, greedy regret)
unmapped: Base arms are partitioned into units; an action is a set of exactly K units (paper's K), and all base arms of selected units are observed
Expected reward r(S,mu) is a general (possibly nonlinear) function of the action and the mean vector, B-Lipschitz in the l1 norm over the base arms of S (Assumption 2); monotonicity is not assumed
Regret is measured against the solution of the Greedy offline oracle applied to the true means (greedy regret), not against the true optimum
The learner knows the reward function r and the unit structure (needed by the Greedy oracle)
settings.definition_quote: The environment contains $m$ base arms ... Each arm $i \in [m]$ is associated with a distribution $D_i$ on $[0,1]$. ... the agent selects an action $S_t \in \cS=\set{S \subseteq \cU: |S|= K}$ ... semi-bandit feedback ... $R_g(T) = \EE{\sum_{t=1}^T \max\set{r(S_g,\mu)- r(S_t,\mu),0} }$

settings.name_in_paper: PMC problem instance of Figure 1 (lower bound)
unmapped: Probabilistic maximum coverage reward on a fixed bipartite graph with 4 left nodes (units) and 2 right nodes
Regret is measured against the Greedy oracle's solution (greedy regret)
settings.definition_quote: We take the following PMC problem (shown in Figure 1) as the instance ... The action size is set to $K=2$ ... where we assume $0<\Delta\le 0.04$ ... we also assume the output of each base arm in each round is exactly its mean.
